newsitem.title: EU: COMMISSION ADOPTS SECOND CHANCE SCHOOLS PROJECTS.
newsitem.headline: COMMISSION ADOPTS SECOND CHANCE SCHOOLS PROJECTS.

text.p: EUROPEAN COMMISSION PRESS RELEASE: IP/97/530
DOCUMENT DATE: JUNE 18, 1997
"Second chance" schools will start in Autumn

In 1995 the European Commission proposed in its White Paper "Teaching and Learning : towards the Learning Society" the idea of "second chance schools" - pilot projects aiming at fighting against social exclusion. These schools enter into their concrete phase in Autumn. Five of them - in Marseilles (France), Bilbao (Spain), Hameenlinna (Finland), Catania (Italy) and Halle (Germany) - will open their doors in September-October, four others - Nikea (Greece), Ribe (Denmark), Seixal (Portugal) and Heerlen (Netherlands) - will do so at the end of the year. This is what Edith Cresson, Commissionner in charge of Research, Education, Training and Youth, will announce today during a working meeting in Brussels with representatives of each of these cities.

Supported by the European Union, local and regional authorities as well as other local actors (associations, private companies, training centres, universities...), the "second chance schools" aim to give young people excluded from the classical school system a new opportunity for reinsertion by means of appropriate educational methods using in particular the new multimedia technologies. They are pilot projects which can be pursued and further developed by the Member States if they so wish. Proposed by the Commission in 1995 in its White paper "Teaching and Learning : towards the Learning society", the idea of second chance schools has already inspired comparable projects in some Member States.

The working meeting held today in Brussels with Mme Edith Cresson will give the representatives of the cities selected by the Commission the opportunity to introduce "their" school and its educational project. These representatives include : Josu Ortundo Larrea, Mayor of Bilbao, Jean-Claude Gaudin, Mayor of Marseilles, Veikko Syyrakki, Mayor of Haemeenlinna, Vassilis Trapalis, Mayor of Nikea and Laurits Tornaes, Mayor of Ribe. Nine "second chance schools" should open their doors before the end of the year : five in September-October (Bilbao, Catania, Halle, Hameenlinna and Marseilles) and four at the end of the year (Nikea, Ribe, Seixal, Heerlen) - see annex.
The characteristics of each project depend to a large extent on local, regional and national needs and circumstances but a few key elements are to be noted:

- a strong partnership between the local authority, social services, institutions and public and private sector employers, the latter in particular with a view to trainership, mentoring and the actual recruitment of the young persons.
- a teaching method that will be modeled on the needs, aspirations and capacities of each individual and that will promote his/her active and constructive learning
- a central role for learning and training in the field of informatics and new technologies,
- a focus on deprived urban areas where the young unemployed people live

The financing of each project will be supported mainly by the local partners, and the rest by the European Union, in particular the Structural Funds, the education programme Socrates and the training programme Leonardo. The European Commission will also provide each project with technical assistance, to help finalise the financing plan.
The working meeting will take place in tne Centre Borschette at 3.15 pm. It will be accessible to all journalists who are interested.
BILBAO, Spain

Eneko Astigarraga Prospektiker Don Leandro 320800 ZarautzPais Vasco tel 34-43-835704 fax: 34-43-132520
Target group : 150 young persons over 16 years old. The number could progressively grow to 400 persons.

Milestones : Definitive physical location: May 1997 Selection and training of trainers: May-September 1997 Selection and progressive admission of students: September 1997 Start up of the first courses: October-December 1997

Social/econ context : Declining traditional industries as steel and shipbuilding. No less than 25,7 % of the active population is unemployed (41,800 in total) of which 70% more than a year. Youth unemployment is 57 % In the population group 15 - 19 approx 10 % had no primary school diploma's and by the final year of compulsory education in Bilbao the failure rate is 27 to 30 %.

Pedagogic approach : Needs adressed on two basic axes:(1) personal and social development,(2) development of capabilities required to handle working life combination of individual approach and insertion into a group as socializing and motivating environment co-operation with various institutions to look at personal, family, social and health problems that may lie behind the 'school' problem active not passive consumption; and self-assessment based evaluation of progress made, 'constructive learning' flexible curriculum and time-table educators as mediators attention for languages, new information technologies and computers 'teaching contract' some elements of the programme inside businesses guidance, character, attitude and self-esteem development premises and image of the school less scholastic, close to the natural environment of the youngsters yet still free of parental control.
Management : Lan Ekintza Bilbao SA

Partnership: European Software Institute based in metropolitan Bilbao Bilbao Metropoli-30 association (RDA with 100 members) Basque government Province of Bizkaia Prospektiker (research)Private companies employers organisations Universities neigbourhoood associations caritas and other NGO'sAll to be placed in a working group and providing input

Urban regeneration dimension :The school will be placed in 'Bilbao la veja', the old harbor area of Bilbao, which is now characterised by a multitude of urban problems: urban degradation, pollution, unemployment, poverty, prostitution.The school would be one element of a broader strategy to rejuvenate the area, through refurbishment of buildings, development of small enterprises etc.

Employment prospects: Relations with companies will be formalised in "co-operation agreements". This can involve training places, job profile input into courses or recruitment 'preferences'. The companies can then get a 'label' recognising them as partner.

Recognition diplomas: New techniques and instruments as 'student profiles', 'credit cards' to be used to obtain external recognition in particular by employers. Employers from their side will be involved in communicating job profiles so that courses will reflect the demand side of the labour market.
